question: Who carried Jesus' cross?
summary: John 19:17 has Jesus carry his own cross to Golgotha — explicitly, *bastazōn heautō ton stauron*. Matthew 27:32, Mark 15:21, and Luke 23:26 have Simon the Cyrenian compelled to carry the cross for him. One gospel has Jesus do it himself; the other three have him hand off the load.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the accounts as one sequence: Jesus carried the cross at first, and Simon was compelled only when exhaustion stopped him.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses it flatly: John has Jesus bear his own cross, while the three Synoptics have Simon of Cyrene carry it — the texts simply name different bearers.

pd_work.note: Clarke keys the harmonization to this passage: Jesus bore the cross alone at first (John), and Simon of Cyrene was compelled only when weakness stopped him (the Synoptics) — one sequence on the road to Golgotha.

link.title: CARM: Did Jesus or Simon of Cyrene carry the cross?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment resolving John 19:17 and the Synoptics by sequence — Jesus bore it until unable, then Simon assisted.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: He bore it all alone first; when he could no longer carry the whole through weakness, occasioned by the ill usage he had received, Simon, a Cyrenian, helped him to carry it
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The most direct harmonization: Jesus carried the cross alone at first (John), and Simon was compelled only when weakness made him unable to continue (the Synoptics) — one sequence, not two accounts in conflict.
